Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the latency looks promising for our clinical summarization pilot. Our Legal team needs two items to complete the onboarding checklist: a signed CPRA/US-state privacy attestation that Redwood will act only as a "service provider"/processor under the CPRA (no sale, no behavioral advertising), and a current list of subprocessors with an expected notification timeline for new third parties.

- Confirmation that logs/telemetry used for product improvement will be covered by the attestation and not used to build derivative models of Acme customer data.

Can you get us a draft attestation and the subprocessor export by EOD Thursday (11/12)? We are targeting an internal approval meeting on 11/15.

Jasmine —

We can provide a concise attestation. Draft attached (redwood-cpra-attestation-v1.pdf). Key points included:
- Redwood confirms it acts as a "service provider"/processor for CPRA/US state privacy law purposes and will not "sell" Personal Information as defined by those laws.
- Redwood will process data only per Acme's documented instructions and the DPA; any telemetry used to improve product will be aggregated and deidentified and cannot be used to build customer-specific derivative models.
- Subprocessor onboarding: Redwood provides notice of new subprocessors 30 days in advance by default; for high-risk subprocessors (e.g., new AI model vendors), we offer a 45-day window and can provide the SoW and security questionnaire.

On subprocessors: Vanessa, can you generate the CSV with columns (vendor, function, country, last_subprocessor_review_date)? I added a column for "high_risk" that we can populate for AI/analytics vendors. I also attached a small retention matrix we can use if Acme asks about retention for MAU or logs (mau-retention-matrix.xlsx).

If Acme insists on 10-day notice instead of 30, we should push back — it's operationally risky. Suggest we offer 14 days for non-production, 30 days for production-facing subprocessors.

Neha
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
